title: Why Double Sanitary Tees Fail in Horizontal Drainage
description: Installing a standard double sanitary tee on horizontal drain lines often leads to cross-discharge and blockages. When water discharges from one side, it can shoot straight across into the opposite fixture arm rather than flowing down the main stack. To prevent crossover contamination and self-siphoning, professional codes require a double combination wye and one-eighth bend or a double fixture fitting for back-to-back horizontal drainage connections. Choosing the correct directional fitting ensures smooth gravity flow and preserves proper atmospheric venting for both fixtures.

Why Double Sanitary Tees Fail in Horizontal Drainage

Installing a standard double sanitary tee on horizontal drain lines often leads to cross-discharge and blockages. When water discharges from one side, it can shoot straight across into the opposite fixture arm rather than flowing down the main stack. To prevent crossover contamination and self-siphoning, professional codes require a double combination wye and one-eighth bend or a double fixture fitting for back-to-back horizontal drainage connections. Choosing the correct directional fitting ensures smooth gravity flow and preserves proper atmospheric venting for both fixtures.
